security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting or package names, not Ruby shell execution. Real risk remains because the skill uses the external belt CLI to run arbitrary Python and includes network-capable examples. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed SKILL.md file.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the exact belt app run workflow or document why full belt access is required.
Warn users not to send secrets, credentials, or private data into code executed by the hosted service.
Pin trusted install sources and explain that web requests from Python leave the sandbox.

content.user_title: Run Python Workloads in a Hosted Sandbox
content.value_statement: Agents often need Python libraries without changing the local machine. This skill runs Python through a hosted sandbox with common data, web, media, and document packages.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python code through the inference.sh belt CLI.
Uses common libraries for data analysis, plotting, scraping, and media processing.
Returns files saved under the documented outputs directory.
Supports API calls and public web requests from executed Python code.
Offers default and high-memory execution variants.
limitations: Execution depends on the external belt CLI and inference.sh service.
The documented environment is CPU-only and not suited for GPU workloads.
Interactive notebooks and long-running services are outside the documented workflow.
Sensitive data should not be sent without explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Analyze Data Without Local Setup
use_cases.description: Load small datasets, calculate summaries, and produce charts without installing Python packages locally.

use_cases.title: Prepare Media Assets
use_cases.description: Resize images, create short videos, or convert document assets in a hosted Python environment.

use_cases.title: Test Automation Scripts
use_cases.description: Run short Python scripts to transform files, call APIs, or validate automation ideas.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Python Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to calculate summary statistics for this small table and explain the result in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Data Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to analyze this dataset, save a chart, and return the main findings.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Public Web Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to fetch a public web page, extract the page title, and summarize visible metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Media Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to resize these images, create output files, and report each generated artifact.

output_examples.input: A sales table needs a quick visual summary.
output_examples.output: The response includes row counts, top category, trend notes, and a returned chart image.

output_examples.input: A public web page must be checked for its title and metadata.
output_examples.output: The response lists the page title, detected metadata, status code, and scraping notes.

output_examples.input: Several images need resizing for a report.
output_examples.output: The response returns resized image files and a brief processing summary.

best_practices: Use public or synthetic data unless the user explicitly approves sensitive input.
Set short timeouts for small jobs and increase them only for media or large data.
Save artifacts under outputs so the sandbox can return them.
anti_patterns: Do not send secrets, tokens, or private customer data into remote Python execution.
Do not use this skill for long-running services or interactive notebooks.
Do not scrape sites without permission or without checking their terms.

faq.question: Does this run Python locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the belt CLI to run code through the inference.sh hosted sandbox.

faq.question: Can it access the network?
faq.answer: Yes. Examples include HTTP requests, so users should treat network egress as possible.

faq.question: Can it use GPU libraries?
faq.answer: No. The documented environment is CPU-only.

faq.question: How are files returned?
faq.answer: Files saved in the outputs directory are detected and returned by the sandbox.

faq.question: Is it safe for secrets?
faq.answer: No. Avoid secrets or private data because code and outputs pass through an external service.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
